materialBoundaries.counterexample: A freely supplied origin could relabel a generic kill as STOP or CANCEL and fabricate a valid cleanup sequence.
materialBoundaries.invariant: A kill-origin label must be issued by the actual source call site and must not be supplied by an external string, environment variable, API field, or serialized input.
materialBoundaries.legitimateControl: The patch uses an unexported typed origin and six fixed private wrappers around exactly three Process.Kill calls; unknown or mismatched origins set bounded=false.

materialBoundaries.counterexample: Adding origin to the exported JSON shape or changing legacy kinds would invalidate old readers, evidence pins, and four-mode S2 contracts.
materialBoundaries.invariant: Existing native recovery consumers must retain the legacy four-field call DTO, ordering, and generic KILL kinds.
materialBoundaries.legitimateControl: Raw events are stored internally; labNativeRecoveryReadCalls copies only the original call under the same mutex, one row per event. The legacy call struct and event snapshot blocks are byte-identical and old V5/BOUND pins are unchanged.
materialBoundaries.runtimeRoot: labNativeRecoveryReadCalls and existing native completion/recovery readers

materialBoundaries.legitimateControl: All active producers and readers use the same fixed schemas; old versions remain negative fixtures, closures include all three new Go sources, and Python model suites exercise coordinated and single-sided schema rewrites.

materialBoundaries.legitimateControl: encoded_secret_variants, build_forbidden, and fence_outputs are byte-identical; safe_report_outputs only advances fixed schemas; no origin is serialized in the legacy DTO; authn, store, RBAC, raw HTTP bodies, index, and authority sources are unchanged.
